title: Best Platform to Sell Digital Products in India (2026)

description: Compare the best platforms to sell digital products in India in 2026. Explore pricing, fees, features and find the right platform for your creator business.

imageAlt: Illustrative guide to choosing a platform for selling digital products in India

blocks.text: Disclosure: CloverLoop publishes this guide and is one of the nine platforms compared. We applied the same criteria and fee method to every platform, used competitor pricing and help pages where available, cross-checked figures against recent independent reviews, and marked figures we could not confirm as "Check current pricing."

Indian creators package what they know into guitar tabs, exam notes, Notion templates, Lightroom presets, planners and ebooks. Once a digital product exists, each extra copy costs almost nothing to deliver, so the selling platform affects how much of every sale you keep.

Four factors matter most: platform and payment-provider charges, convenient payment options for Indian buyers, how files reach buyers, and whether you retain the customer relationship. This guide compares nine platforms on those factors, with fee calculations you can check yourself.
Quick Answer: Which Is the Best Platform to Sell Digital Products in India?

CloverLoop is our recommended primary platform for many Indian creators. Its Free and Creator plans have no monthly fee; Free charges no platform fee, while Creator charges 4%. Gumroad, Payhip and Etsy can suit overseas selling, and Ownstreet's 0% platform-fee model may cost less at higher volumes.

Why CloverLoop leads this comparison: Free and Creator cost ₹0 per month; Free has a 0% platform fee; Pro Creator costs ₹2,999 per month for a 0% platform fee; Creator and Pro Creator include unlimited paid and free listings; the platform focuses on ebooks, PDFs, templates, presets, printables and music resources; and each creator has a dedicated storefront rather than a marketplace listing.

Other platforms fit particular needs: Gumroad for overseas buyers, Etsy for marketplace discovery abroad, Instamojo for payment links and Indian commerce, and SuperProfile for Instagram-led selling. The fee analysis below shows where each model costs less.
How We Evaluated the Platforms

We assessed each platform against ten criteria, giving the most weight to affordability, commercial sustainability and fit for Indian creators: platform transaction fees; monthly subscription costs; Indian payment compatibility, including Razorpay, PayU, UPI and INR payouts; INR pricing; digital product support; storefront versus marketplace experience; product listing flexibility; scalability; ease of setup, including KYC and GSTIN requirements; and overall creator economics on a ₹499 sale.
Figures were checked on 5 November 2026 against official pricing and help pages where accessible, and against dated independent reviews where they were not. Unconfirmed items are marked.

Key terms: a platform transaction fee is what the selling platform keeps from each sale. A payment gateway fee is charged by a provider such as Razorpay to collect money; it is separate, and 18% GST applies to it in India. A storefront is your own page where buyers browse and buy. A merchant of record is the entity legally selling to the buyer and handling sales-tax collection on your behalf.
Comparison Table: Best Platforms to Sell Digital Products in India
Subscription and platform transaction fees are separate. Gateway or card-processing charges are extra unless stated as bundled.

CloverLoop — ₹0 monthly on Free and Creator; ₹2,999 on Pro Creator. Free: 0%; Creator: 4%; Pro Creator: 0%. Best for creators building a regular digital-product business; offers unlimited listings on Creator and Pro Creator and a dedicated storefront.

Instamojo — ₹0 on Lite, ₹6,999 per year on Starter and ₹14,999 per year on Growth. Digital-goods fees are listed as 10% + ₹3 on Lite and Starter or 5% + ₹3 on Growth, with gateway bundled and GST extra. Best for payment links and Indian commerce.

Ownstreet — ₹0, ₹299 or ₹799 monthly with a 0% platform fee; Razorpay charges are separate. Best for combining a bio link and store.

Linktree — check current pricing. Paid digital products are not offered to India-based sellers. Best for link-in-bio management.
Individual Platform Reviews
1. CloverLoop – Our Top Pick for Indian Digital Creators

CloverLoop gives independent creators a dedicated, shareable storefront for ebooks, PDFs, templates, presets, printables and music resources. It is not a marketplace: creators bring their audience from Instagram, YouTube or a newsletter, and payment arrangements stay with the creator.

Plans: Free costs ₹0, charges no platform fee, and includes one paid and five free listings per account, lifetime. Creator costs ₹0 and charges 4%, with unlimited paid and free listings. Pro Creator costs ₹2,999 per month and charges 0%, with unlimited paid and free listings. Monthly prices exclude applicable GST. Payment gateway charges from Razorpay or another provider are separate.

CloverLoop is designed around digital products, has no fixed subscription on Creator, publishes platform fees separately from gateway charges, and offers a [creator earnings calculator](https://cloverloop.in/pricing#earnings-calculator). Its storefront lets creators present products directly to buyers.

Plan prices are in rupees, and the cost structure scales with sales instead of charging rent in slow months. The [GST guide](https://cloverloop.in/resources/do-you-need-gst-registration-to-sell-online) and [Razorpay UPI guide](https://cloverloop.in/resources/accept-upi-payments-digital-products-razorpay) address common setup questions for Indian creators.

CloverLoop is a newer platform with less track record than Gumroad, Payhip or Instamojo. Its public pages do not list supported file types, upload limits, checkout methods such as UPI, payout timing or integrations; confirm these before committing a large catalogue. There is no marketplace, so discovery depends on your own promotion.
Best for: first-time creators, musicians and educators selling tabs, notes and guides, and anyone who wants ₹0 fixed cost while testing demand. [Explore CloverLoop](https://cloverloop.in/).
2. Gumroad – Best for International Digital Product Selling

Gumroad is a well-known tool for selling downloads, with fast setup and an established international creator community. It has no monthly plan and charges 10% + $0.50 on direct sales and 30% when a new buyer finds you through Discover; the Discover fee includes processing. The 10% + $0.50 excludes card processing (2.9% + $0.30) and PayPal fees on direct sales. Reviewers report a reduced rate above $20,000 in monthly sales; check current pricing.

Fees are in dollars, so the fixed $0.50 weighs heavily on low-priced products: about ₹47.50 on a ₹499 sale at ₹95 per dollar. Gumroad help pages are reported to list India for INR bank payouts and UPI for buyers in India; confirm both and the minimum payout balance before relying on them. Best for creators with a mostly overseas audience or an existing Gumroad following.
3. Payhip – Best for Simple Digital Download Stores

Payhip offers a storefront for downloads, memberships and courses, with the same features on every plan. Free Forever is $0 + 5%; Plus is $29 per month + 2%; Pro is $99 per month + 0%. Payment-processor charges are separate on all plans.

Payhip's help centre lists Razorpay and PayU for Indian sellers. Through Razorpay, buyers can see UPI, cards, net banking and wallets. Payhip states Razorpay payments reach sellers immediately and its own fees are billed to their card at month-end. Stripe is reported to be invite-only for new Indian merchants.

Subscriptions are priced in dollars: Plus is roughly ₹2,755 and Pro roughly ₹9,405 at ₹95 per dollar. Plus only becomes cheaper than Free above about $967 (roughly ₹92,000) in monthly sales. Best for creators selling to Indian and overseas buyers who are comfortable connecting their own Razorpay account.
4. Instamojo – Best for Payment Links and Indian Commerce

Instamojo is an established Indian payments and online-store provider with a built-in gateway. Store plans are Lite at ₹0, Starter at ₹6,999 per year and Growth at ₹14,999 per year, with GST extra. Its support page lists digital goods at 10% + ₹3 on Lite and Starter and 5% + ₹3 on Growth, excluding 18% GST on the fee; payment processing is bundled. Payment-link pricing differs, so check current pricing.

Digital goods cost more than physical goods, and store tools such as cart, cash on delivery and shipping are primarily built for physical commerce. Third-party reviews put settlement at about three working days. Best for sellers who want payment links and an Indian gateway, or who already run an Instamojo store. See [CloverLoop vs Instamojo](https://cloverloop.in/compare/cloverloop-vs-instamojo).
5. SuperProfile – Best for Social Media-Led Creator Monetisation

SuperProfile combines a link-in-bio storefront with Instagram DM automation, courses, bookings and communities. For Indian creators it manages payments centrally, including UPI, cards and buy-now-pay-later after KYC, with next-day (T+1) payouts according to SuperProfile.

The free Starter plan cannot sell products. Creator costs ₹99 for the first month and ₹499 per month after that, plus a 5% platform fee per sale for Indian creators. Its help centre reportedly adds GST on that fee; check current pricing. Creators outside India pay $29 per month with no platform fee and connect their own Stripe or PayPal. The ₹499 subscription applies in slow months too. Best for Instagram-first creators who will use DM automation and want centrally handled payments. See [CloverLoop vs SuperProfile](https://cloverloop.in/compare/cloverloop-vs-superprofile).
6. GetSauce – An Alternative for Indian Creators

GetSauce is an India-based marketplace with category browsing, free sign-up, advertised UPI support and instant payouts. Its live pricing page lists Creator at ₹0 with a 15% transaction fee, and Creator Pro at ₹89 per month (₹599 per year) with a 10% fee, ranking and a verification badge. Other pages advertise a 5% fee and "no fees on Pro," so check current pricing in your dashboard. Gateway treatment is not stated.

The pricing-page percentages are higher than most alternatives, conflicting fee statements make planning harder, and GetSauce is a younger platform. Best for creators who want in-India marketplace discovery and accept a higher percentage in return.
7. Ownstreet – Best for Its Bio-Link and Storefront Approach

Ownstreet combines bio links and a digital store on one page. Checkout runs on Razorpay and shows UPI, cards and net banking. Sellers can receive payouts to a bank account using bank details and PAN or connect their own Razorpay keys.

The platform fee is 0% on every plan; Razorpay gateway charges are separate. Free costs ₹0 and allows one live paid product and up to five completed paid sales. Pro is ₹299 per month with unlimited products, email capture, reviews and branding removed. Pro Max is ₹799 per month with a custom domain, GST invoices, coupons and team seats. Ownstreet says bank credit typically takes two to three working days.

After five paid sales the Free plan stops, so active sellers may need a flat monthly fee. Ownstreet branding shows on Free, and it is a newer platform with founder-led support. Best for creators who want one URL for links and a shop and expect enough sales for a flat fee to beat a percentage. Against CloverLoop Creator, that crossover is about ₹7,475 in monthly sales.
8. Etsy – Best for Marketplace Discovery

Etsy's strength is built-in buyer search traffic, especially for printables, planners and templates. Etsy charges $0.20 per listing and a 6.5% transaction fee. For sellers with an Indian bank account, its payments policy lists a processing fee of 5% + ₹25 per sale. Etsy Help mentions a one-time $10 setup fee for Indian sellers. An Offsite Ads fee applies only to orders that arrive through Etsy's own ads.

Etsy Help states that Indian sellers must verify a GSTIN and use Payoneer, and that new Indian shops can currently sell only internationally. Etsy pays out in US dollars on Mondays, so Payoneer conversion and withdrawal charges apply. Best for GST-registered creators targeting overseas buyers who search Etsy for printables and templates.
9. Linktree – Best for Link-in-Bio Management

Linktree is a link-management tool first and a commerce tool second. A link page and a platform that handles checkout, delivery and refunds are different products. Its help centre, updated 14 October 2026, lists countries where creators can sell digital products; India is not on the list, and selling requires a Pro or Premium plan. Where available, Linktree publishes seller fees of 9% on Pro and 0% on Premium, plus Stripe processing. Plan prices are in dollars; check current pricing.
Indian creators cannot currently sell paid digital products through Linktree, but a Linktree page can still link out to a storefront. Best for managing many links in one place.
What Happens to Your Earnings? A ₹499 Product, 10 Sales a Month

Assumptions: one product at ₹499 with ten sales monthly gives ₹4,990 gross. Platform fees are shown before GST. Where a platform does not bundle the gateway, we add Razorpay's standard domestic rate of 2% + 18% GST, or 2.36% (₹117.76 on ₹4,990); your agreement may differ. Dollar charges are converted at an illustrative ₹95 per $1. "Retained" means before income tax, GST on your own sales, refunds and chargebacks.
CloverLoop plans

On ₹4,990 gross monthly revenue, Free has ₹0 monthly fee and ₹0 platform charges. Creator has ₹0 monthly fee and ₹199.60 platform charges at 4%. Pro Creator has a ₹2,999 monthly fee and ₹0 in platform charges at 0%. Gateway fees and applicable taxes are additional.

Pro Creator is not economical at ten sales. Its ₹2,999 monthly subscription and 0% platform fee cost less than Creator's 4% platform fee above about ₹74,975 in monthly sales, before applicable taxes and provider charges.
All platforms, same method

Estimated total charges and retained amounts on ₹4,990 gross, before any applicable GST on CloverLoop subscriptions: CloverLoop Free, ₹117.76 total and ₹4,872.24 retained; CloverLoop Creator, ₹317.36 total and ₹4,672.64 retained; Payhip Free, ₹367.26 total and ₹4,622.74 retained; Ownstreet Pro, ₹416.76 total and ₹4,573.24 retained; Instamojo Lite for digital goods, ₹529 platform/gateway fees plus ₹95.22 GST, leaving ₹4,461 before GST on the fee.

Further estimates: GetSauce Creator Pro, ₹588 total and ₹4,402 retained before any unstated gateway charge; SuperProfile Creator, ₹748.50 plus ₹44.91 GST, leaving ₹4,241.50 before any gateway charge; GetSauce Creator, ₹748.50 and ₹4,241.50 before any gateway charge; Etsy for Indian export sales, ₹1,013.85 and ₹3,976.15 before Payoneer charges; Gumroad direct sale, ₹1,403.71 and ₹3,586.29; CloverLoop Pro Creator, ₹3,116.76 and ₹1,873.24 before applicable GST on the subscription. Linktree does not offer paid digital products to India-based sellers.

Ownstreet's Free plan covers only the first five completed paid sales, so ten sales a month need Pro. Payhip Plus and Pro and Instamojo Growth are not shown because their subscriptions cost more than they save at ten sales; Gumroad's reported high-volume rate applies only far above this volume. Etsy assumes a $0.20 listing renewal on each sale and excludes its one-time $10 setup fee and 0.5% tax collected at source. Gumroad assumes card processing of 2.9% + $0.30. GST shown for Instamojo and SuperProfile is 18% of the platform fee.
Where the arithmetic changes

At ten sales a month, CloverLoop Free keeps the most because it has no platform fee, and Ownstreet Free stops after five paid sales. Free is limited to one paid product listing; Creator removes that limit at 4%.

Ownstreet Pro costs less than CloverLoop Creator once monthly sales pass ₹7,475 (₹299 ÷ 4%), and less than CloverLoop Pro Creator at every volume. Choose based on expected sales, how many products you sell, and which storefront and payment arrangement you prefer—not on the headline percentage alone.
Which Platform Should You Choose?

For starting a digital-product business in India, consider CloverLoop: ₹0 monthly and no platform fee on Free. For a low-cost creator-commerce model, compare CloverLoop with Ownstreet Pro above about ₹7,475 monthly sales. CloverLoop supports ebooks and downloadable resources. Ownstreet puts a bio link and store on one page.

For international digital-product selling, consider Gumroad. For a simple download storefront, consider Payhip. For payment links and Indian commerce, consider Instamojo. For social media-led monetisation, consider SuperProfile. For marketplace discovery, compare Etsy for overseas sales (GSTIN required) with GetSauce in India. Linktree is a link hub, but does not offer paid digital products in India.
Frequently Asked Questions
Which is the best platform to sell digital products in India in 2026?

CloverLoop is our recommended primary platform for many Indian creators starting out: Free and Creator have no monthly fee, Free has no platform fee, Creator charges 4%, and creators get a dedicated storefront. Higher-volume sellers should compare Ownstreet's flat-fee model; sellers targeting overseas buyers can consider Gumroad or Payhip.
Can I sell digital products online without a website?

Yes. Hosted platforms such as CloverLoop, Payhip, Gumroad and Ownstreet give you a storefront link to share in your Instagram or YouTube bio. You upload the file and set a price. You still need a way to collect payments, which in India usually involves KYC with a gateway or the platform's own payment system.
Which platform has the lowest transaction fees in India?

Among the platforms reviewed, Ownstreet lists a 0% platform fee on all plans, with gateway charges separate and a Free plan capped at five paid sales. CloverLoop Free also has a 0% platform fee and a lifetime listing limit. Compare total cost, including subscriptions and gateway charges, rather than the headline percentage.
Can I sell ebooks and PDFs online in India?

Yes. CloverLoop, Payhip, Instamojo, SuperProfile and Ownstreet support ebook and PDF sales. Check supported file types and size limits, how buyers receive the file, and who pays payment charges. You must own or have permission to distribute the content you sell.
Is Gumroad suitable for Indian creators?

It can be, with caveats. Gumroad help pages are reported to list India for INR bank payouts and UPI for buyers in India. The cost is 10% + $0.50 per direct sale, card processing on top, and 30% on Discover sales. Fixed dollar fees weigh heavily on products under about ₹1,000.
What is the best alternative to Gumroad in India?

It depends on what you want to change. CloverLoop offers lower platform fees and a dedicated storefront, Payhip offers similar simplicity with Razorpay support, and Instamojo, SuperProfile and Ownstreet focus on Indian payments. See [CloverLoop vs Gumroad](https://cloverloop.in/compare/cloverloop-vs-gumroad) and [CloverLoop vs Payhip](https://cloverloop.in/compare/cloverloop-vs-payhip).
Do I need GST registration to sell digital products in India?

It depends on your circumstances. GST registration thresholds differ for goods and services and by state, and some cases require registration regardless of turnover. Etsy requires a GSTIN from Indian sellers. Check the [GST Council's registration guidance](https://www.gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/e-version-gst-flyers/Registration_under_GST_Law_new.pdf) or ask a qualified tax professional. See our [GST guide for creators](https://cloverloop.in/resources/do-you-need-gst-registration-to-sell-online).
How much does it cost to sell digital products online?

Costs have three layers: platform subscription and per-sale fees, payment gateway charges (Razorpay's standard domestic rate is 2% + 18% GST, or 2.36%), and taxes. In the ₹499 example, platform and gateway charges for ten sales ranged from about ₹118 on CloverLoop Free to about ₹1,404 on Gumroad, excluding paid plans whose subscriptions pay off only at higher volumes.
What is the difference between a platform fee and a payment gateway fee?

A platform fee is what the selling platform keeps. A gateway fee is what the payment provider, such as Razorpay, charges to move money. CloverLoop, Ownstreet and Payhip keep them separate; Instamojo bundles them. GST at 18% applies to Indian gateway fees.
Can I sell digital products through Instagram?

Yes. Put your storefront link in your bio and Stories, or use a tool such as SuperProfile that can send a checkout link when someone comments. The sale happens on your storefront or payment page, not inside Instagram. Linktree can route traffic, but paid digital products are not offered to India-based sellers.
Which platform is best for beginners selling digital products?

For one product and no upfront cost, CloverLoop Free has no platform fee and includes one paid product listing. Ownstreet Free allows five paid sales before an upgrade, and SuperProfile requires a paid plan before you can sell. Read our [beginner's guide](https://cloverloop.in/resources/how-to-sell-digital-products-online).
Is CloverLoop a marketplace?

No. CloverLoop is designed around independent creator storefronts rather than a central catalogue, so you bring your own audience. Marketplaces such as Etsy and GetSauce offer built-in browsing traffic but charge more per sale and set their own rules.
Conclusion

The best platform depends on your business model, audience, geography and sales volume. Overseas sellers are well served by Gumroad, Payhip and Etsy. Instagram-led sellers may value SuperProfile's automation. Creators who expect high, steady sales should test whether Ownstreet's flat-fee model saves them money.

For creators starting or growing a digital-product business in India, CloverLoop is our recommended primary platform. It combines a digital-product focus, a dedicated storefront and no fixed cost on Free and Creator. Read the [pricing details](https://cloverloop.in/pricing), then [visit CloverLoop](https://cloverloop.in/) to see whether it fits your products.
